label: rem:witt-lift-qou
title: Role in the QOU lifting theorem
html:
The skew-Poisson integration theorem is a statement over a field k of characteristic p. Its bearing on the p-adic realisation is limited, and this remark records what it does and does not supply.

  1. It supplies a construction over k: from a strongly filtered, strongly multiplicative Poisson structure on the splay of the distribution algebras of a commutative geometric formal group, it builds a bialgebra U with a PBW basis, which the source identifies with \mathrm{Dist}(G) for a non-commutative formal group G over k.
  2. It does not supply a Witt vector lift. No lift of G or of H to W(k) or \mathbb{Z}_p is constructed in the source, so the passage from the \mathbb{F}_p fibre algebra to a \mathbb{Q}_p fibre algebra is not a consequence of it.
  3. Strong multiplicativity is a compatibility between \pi and the comultiplication of the free product. It is not the Frobenius relation (\mathrm{Id}\otimes m)\circ(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{Id}) = \Delta\circ m used in jet prolongation, and the theorem does not prove that relation.

No unit-root F-crystal criterion for integrability appears in the source.
